maqm.review:
CSE445: Machine Learning
This is a traditional ML course that helps you build a solid foundation in the field. It mainly focuses on regression, classification algorithms, and evaluation metrics. Prerequisites include Python, Statistics, and LaTeX, so having a basic grip on these is important.
I took it under MAQm sir. His lectures were mostly based on Aurélien Géron’s ML textbook and StatQuest with Josh Starmer. Topics covered throughout the semester included EDA, preprocessing, regression, classification, SVM, decision trees, ensemble learning, unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, and even a short intro to neural networks.
The course had one surprise quiz, one coding-based ML assignment with a report and viva, a mid and final exam (both allowing a one-sided cheat sheet), and a group project. The question patterns are MCQs, mathematical, and short questions. The project carried significant weight with marks for proposal, progress, final report, demo, and viva. Project Evaluation is done by the Sir, TA and RA. Overall, your grade will depend a lot on the assignment and project, so those are the key parts to focus on. Overall, this course provides a good understanding of ML at the beginner level.

If you value learning over grading, the best choice would be SfR1 Sir.
Reasons:
1. Most of the faculties do not update their Machine Learning Syllabus and do not go in-depth. Imagine you are studying a Machine Learning course and have no idea about Neural Networks. Sounds absurd, right? SfR1 Sir's syllabus is very comprehensive and up-to-date. He even spends one class covering traditional Machine Learning Techniques (the topics most faculties spend two-thirds of a semester on).
2. Unlike all faculties, he doesn't give a project at the end of the semester. Rather, he gives 8-9 assignments (Code + Report). The assignments are group-based and require solid knowledge of the topic (and Python) to complete. The report must be written in LaTeX (he will share the format). Although knowledge of Python beforehand will be beneficial, it's not required. You will be given sufficient time to complete the assignments so you can learn and implement within that duration. So, what's the benefit of this approach compared to a project? The answer is the learning experience. You will complete a topic theoretically and then practically implement that knowledge to solidify your understanding. The report writing experience familiarizes you with LaTeX and helps you grasp the methods of writing a research paper.
3. This course under SfR1 Sir would be highly valuable if you wish to do CSE499 and CSE498R with an AI topic.
Lastly, sir takes class position into consideration while grading. You will get an A if you are in the top 10% of the class.
CSE445 - SfR1 (If you want to learn machine learning in depth)
CSE445 - SFR1 (Without a doubt, he is the best faculty for learning ML).
